_comment: Long-form talking head for YouTube: 1920x1080, 30 fps, captions OFF, graphics as overlays on a full-frame speaker. This is the default format and the one the project skeleton already matches, so almost nothing here is an override - it is written out in full anyway, because a preset you have to diff against a Python skeleton to understand is not a preset.
_usage: Project.create(root, slug, preset) deep-merges this document over the skeleton in vedit/project.py: dicts merge, lists replace wholesale, and project_id / created_utc / schema_version / _computed are dropped. So every key here lands in project.json - including 'layout' and 'cut_profile', which are additive fields the render and cut stages read. Keys beginning with '_' are documentation and MUST be ignored by consumers.
name: longform
description: 16:9 long form. Full-frame speaker, overlay graphics, YouTube loudness, no burned-in captions.
_comment_loudnorm: Copied from presets/platforms.json -> youtube.loudnorm. It is duplicated into the project on creation on purpose: a project that has already been mastered must not silently re-target because someone edited platforms.json afterwards. QC check (f) compares the rendered master against THIS value.
_comment_timebase: Integer 30 fps, not 30000/1001. Intake mandatorily transcodes every source to this CFR rate, which is what makes src_*_frames unambiguous across mixed-rate cameras.
_comment_cut_profile: Names a profile in presets/cut-profiles.json. 'balanced' is the CONTRACT section 8 defaults verbatim - uncalibrated, like everything else in presets/.
_comment_captions: OFF by default. A 16:9 video on a desktop player has YouTube's own CC track and does not autoplay muted, so burned-in captions mostly cost you the lower third. Flip enabled:true when the cut is also going to a muted feed - the preset is ready either way. Note burn_in stays true: if captions are on at all in this pipeline they are burned, because a sidecar .ass is not what gets uploaded.

layout._comment: How the frame is composed. Long form is the trivial case: one full-frame speaker with graphics floated over it. Regions are percentages of the output frame so the block survives a resolution change.

graphics._comment: Graphics float over the speaker rather than owning a region. Anchored to {segment_id, offset_frames} in overlays[], never to an absolute timeline frame, so a re-cut upstream does not desync them.

layout._comment_captions_region: null = the caption preset's own margins decide. Only the band layouts (shortform-explainer) override placement here.

_comment_hook: No text hook. Long form opens on the speaker; a burned-in hook card belongs to the vertical formats.
